description: We are a team of curious minds driven by one mission: to push the boundaries of science and technology for a better future in space. Through innovation, collaboration, and artificial intelligence, we aim to turn complex challenges into meaningful solutions and help make space exploration safer for humanity. Because every great discovery begins where the known ends.
summary: ATHERA is a mobile app with an AI system that monitors an astronaut’s physical and mental health on long space missions, where a reply from Earth can take up to 44 minutes. It reads vital signs (heart rate, oxygen saturation, respiration, body temperature, blood pressure), sleep, stress and radiation, the kind of data wearables already collect. An AI model estimates the astronaut’s health risk for the next two hours as safe, early warning or critical, and the app compares every reading with the astronaut’s own normal baseline. When something changes, it shows which signals moved, explains why, and prepares a short medical summary to send to Earth. It also includes an offline well-being companion (Laila) with a mental-health monitor, an emergency simulator, step-by-step first-aid guidance that adapts to where the astronaut is (cabin, spacewalk, ground), and views of real NASA space-hazard data, so the astronaut stays supported even when the connection to Earth is slow or lost. We trained and tested the model on synthetic data and simulated sensors, and the app also shows real data: ISS radiation measurements and Inspiration4 blood tests. ATHERA is a prototype that supports the astronaut and does not replace doctors. The next step is to connect it to real wearable sensors and validate it with real medical data.
details:
What it does. ATHERA gives astronauts a clear, honest picture of their own health without waiting for Earth. It combines:

  • Vitals monitoring: live heart rate, SpO₂, respiration, temperature and blood pressure, with data-quality checks (it says when data is missing or unreliable instead of guessing).
  • Personal baseline and anomaly detection: each astronaut is compared with their own normal range using robust statistics. It flags unusual or persistent changes and shows trends.
  • AI risk prediction: a machine-learning model estimates the risk level for the next 120 minutes (safe, early warning, critical). The app explains which signals drove the result and reports the model’s accuracy and limits.
  • Mental health (Astro Mind and Laila): daily check-ins feed a well-being score with four support levels. Laila is an offline companion chatbot in English and Arabic with a crisis protocol that escalates to a human. She is not a therapist.
  • Emergency guidance: 11 emergencies (fainting, low oxygen, chest pain, abnormal heart rate, breathing problems, stroke signs, dehydration, heat stress, radiation, severe allergy, psychological crisis). Each has numbered steps, actions to avoid, escalation criteria and sources. The advice changes with the astronaut’s location (spacecraft cabin, spacewalk, ground) and role (the affected astronaut or a crewmate helping). On a spacewalk it never tells an impaired astronaut to move.
  • Mission emergency simulator: 15 scenarios (healthy, faint, fainting, hypoxia, chest pain, abnormal heartbeat, breathing difficulty, stroke signs, heat stress, allergy, psychological distress, critical, radiation, lost astronaut, lost astronaut with degraded navigation) with live charts, an event timeline and a final report. All values are labelled SIMULATED.
  • Real NASA data: ISS radiation dose rates (RadLab) and Inspiration4 crew blood tests, shown with their real units and gaps.
  • Crew and mission control views, SOS, and a body map that explains each organ system.

How it works. The app runs on the device and works offline. Vitals flow into on-device engines (baseline, anomaly detection, data quality, trends, well-being). The risk model runs in a small Python service that the app calls when a connection exists, and the app clearly says when the service is unreachable. The emergency guidance is a fixed knowledge base with sources, not generated text, so the AI never invents medical instructions, doses or diagnoses.

Benefits and goals. Earlier warning of health changes, support when communication with Earth is delayed or lost, attention to mental health alongside physical health, and training value through realistic simulations. The goal is decision support for astronauts and flight surgeons.

Tools and technologies.

  • App: Flutter and Dart (Provider, fl_chart, SQLite), Android APK and web demo.
  • AI service: Python, scikit-learn, FastAPI, pandas, NumPy.
  • Testing and delivery: Flutter and pytest test suites, GitHub Actions CI.
  • Data: synthetic vitals for training, real NASA ISS RadLab radiation data, Inspiration4 blood-test data.
  • Hardware: designed for wearables (such as Astroskin-type sensors). The prototype uses simulated sensors.

Limitations (stated openly). The risk model was trained on synthetic data, not real astronaut data. The first-aid guidance is general reference information that has not been clinically reviewed, and ATHERA is not an official NASA medical system. The real radiation and blood data are not used to train the risk model.
